text: Sift scores your feed with EmbeddingGemma, right in the browser. Version 0.2 brings the side panel, smart caching, and muted keywords.
Under the hood, Sift runs an embedding model locally using WebGPU and Transformers.js. Every post is compared against your chosen categories to produce a relevance score.
Hundreds of posts scroll by every day. Only a handful actually matter to you. Sift finds them.
Here's Hacker News without Sift. An undifferentiated wall of links, no way to tell what's relevant at a glance.

overlay.text: No scoring — every post looks the same

text: With Sift enabled, low-relevance posts are dimmed, matching categories appear as pills, and the score inspector shows exactly why each post ranked the way it did.

text: The side panel is your persistent dashboard. It shows the page score, all 25 categories, muted keywords, and your taste profile.
It stays open while you browse, updating in real time as you navigate between pages.

overlay.text: Side panel — always open while you browse

text: Sift works wherever you read. The same model and the same categories give you consistent scoring across every site.
Here it is on Reddit, scoring posts in r/LocalLLaMA.
And on X, surfacing the signal in your timeline.
On article pages like TechCrunch, the side panel scores the full page content.

overlay.title: Article Scoring
overlay.body: Full page content scored in the side panel

text: Muted keywords let you block the noise. Items matching your keywords fade to near-invisible, and no model inference is wasted on them.
Smart caching means if Sift has seen a post before, it skips the model entirely. An LRU cache for two thousand embeddings gives you instant re-scores on tab switches and infinite scroll.
After labeling ten or more items, Sift builds a contrastive taste profile of your interests.
The radar chart and ranked probes show your top interests by affinity, giving you a clear picture of what Sift has learned about you.

overlay.text: Radar chart + ranked probes — your top interests by affinity

text: The Label Manager lets you filter, edit, and reassign categories. It's your curation tool for building high-quality training data.
Filter by category, polarity, or source. Edit labels inline. Reassign categories with a click.
The training loop ties it all together. Label items as you browse, curate in the Label Manager, export as CSV, fine-tune locally or in Colab, then load the model back into Sift.
Everything runs locally. No backend, no API costs, no data leaves your browser. Privacy first.
Sift is open source under Apache 2.0. Check it out on GitHub.
